# Crop rotation

The vegetable beds are divided in four and each family moves one bed every year: legumes, then leafy crops, then fruiting crops, then roots. Planting the same family in the same soil exhausts specific minerals and lets pests settle in. Beans leave nitrogen behind, which the hungry leafy crops use the following year.

It is the same discipline as a Technical debt review: you cannot keep drawing from the same bed without paying something back. A drawing of the four beds hangs in the shed, with the last three years written in each square.

If a bed shows disease, skip the family for four seasons and sow a green manure instead.
